class: Any adapter that reads a JSON reply with the default number parser turns every price, margin and charge into a binary float before it becomes a Decimal, so values like 291444.67000000004 enter the money path and rupee totals pick up representation error.
mechanism: Kite's REST replies carry money as JSON numbers that are not exactly representable (e.g. /margins/basket initial total 291444.67000000004, /charges/orders total 32.962115749999995); json.loads gives floats, and Decimal(float) keeps the binary error.
fix: Every Kite REST reply is parsed with json.loads(..., parse_float=Decimal, parse_int=int) (or the equivalent in the HTTP client) at the adapter boundary, and a test feeds the real captured replies and asserts type(x) is Decimal with the exact text value.

detection.note: No Kite REST adapter exists yet (W-059 covers the WebSocket's integer paise). The guard is a test over the captured rest-2026-10-08 replies in the REST adapter work item.

occurrences.evidence: two money fields with float tails in two endpoints
